About

A 2.4 kW solar system can cover daily use

See if this system fits your home. A kilowatt-hour (kWh) measures energy used over time. An inverter changes the panels' direct current (DC) into alternating current (AC) for home use.

Your panels may cover 35% of your yearly use. You may pay about $8,200 for a typical system. These are estimates, not a quote or a guarantee. Check local rules and talk with a licensed electrician before you decide.

For a news claim, cite an official source. This example uses a public energy dataset updated in 2026. Check the source and review dates before using a figure for a current decision. See the cited dataset details.

Check the rules and stay safe

  • Get two or three quotes and check whether local rules allow you to mount panels yourself.
  • Follow your area's permit and grid-connection steps.
  • Use fall protection when working at height.
  • A licensed electrician must do every electrical termination.

Estimates are for education. They do not replace local legal advice or an electrician's inspection. Read the terms.

Last reviewed: October 10, 2026

kW
A unit for how much power a system can make at once.
Kilowatt-hour (kWh)
A unit that measures energy use.
Inverter
A device that changes the panels' electricity into a form used in the home.
Direct current (DC)
Electricity that flows in one direction.
Alternating current (AC)
Electricity that changes direction many times each second.
Grid connection
The link between a home system and the local electricity network.
Electrical termination
A safe, finished connection between electrical wires and equipment.
Dataset
A set of information collected and shared for people to check.
